query: An equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy has a simple solid-solution structure and favorable plasticity and machinability but relatively low hardness and strength, while its microstructure and deformation behavior remain insufficiently understood. Under hardness testing and mechanical loading of this starting state, what single intervention could overcome the strength and hardness limitation while retaining its favorable mechanical characteristics? State the proposed intervention, its mechanism, the predicted measurable change relative to the unmodified alloy, its applicable processing and test conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a microstructural and mechanical experiment that could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of a minor amount of boron to the CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy will overcome its strength and hardness limitations while retaining its favorable mechanical characteristics.
generation.material_initial_state: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy with a simple solid-solution structure.
generation.intervention: Addition of a minor amount of boron (e.g., 0.1 at.%) to the alloy.
generation.conditions: The alloy is processed and tested under standard conditions for high-entropy alloys, including appropriate temperature and loading conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: Intergranular precipitation of hexagonal close-packed borides at grain boundaries.
generation.mechanism: The boride precipitation enhances grain boundary cohesion, leading to improved work hardenability and ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased hardness and strength of the alloy, particularly at the grain boundaries, while maintaining its favorable plasticity and machinability.
generation.baseline: The unmodified CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy with its original microstructure and mechanical properties.
generation.boundary: The limit of boron addition beyond which the alloy's microstructure and properties may be negatively affected.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal amount of boron addition and the specific processing conditions required to achieve the desired outcome are uncertain and require further investigation.

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the microstructure and mechanical properties of the boron-modified CoCrFeNiTi alloy with those of the unmodified alloy.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the boron-modified alloy does not exhibit significantly improved hardness and strength compared to the unmodified alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text:
Microstructure and Mechanical Properties of Intergranular Boride Precipitation-Toughened HfMoNbTaTiZr Refractory High-Entropy Alloy

Abstract: AbstractTo develop strong refractory high-entropy alloys for use at elevated temperatures as well as to overcome grain-boundary brittleness, an equimolar HfMoNbTaTiZr alloy was prepared, and a minor amount of boron (0.1 at.%) was added into the alloy. The microstructures of the alloys were characterized, and their macro-to-microscale mechanical properties were measured. The microstructural observations indicated that the matrices of both the alloys were composed of a body-centered cubic solid-solution structure, and the added boron induced the precipitation of hexagonal close-packed borides (most likely the (Hf, Zr)B2) at the grain boundaries. The modulus and hardness of differently oriented grains were about equivalent, suggesting a diminished anisotropy, and many small slips occurred on multiple {110} planes. While the hardness of the matrix was not increased, the intergranular precipitation of the borides markedly raised the hardness of the grain boundaries.
